n.quote:
A total of 240 undergraduate students from the University of California, Los Angeles (73

male and 167 female) averaging 20.7 years of age participated in the experiment. ... we compared recall for Rp- versus

Nrp items in Conditions 1 and 3 (where the test did not occur after a block of relearning) to that

obtained for these two types of items in Conditions 2 and 4 (where the test occurred after a block

of relearning).

notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a complete-looking 25-page primary research manuscript (title page, abstract, Method, Results, Discussion, references, footnote, tables and figures). Title and authors Benjamin C. Storm, Elizabeth Ligon Bjork, and Robert A. Bjork match the neutral original reference. SOURCE_URL identifies a UCLA Bjork lab PDF named SBB_JEPLMC_final.pdf. DOI, publication year and journal bibliographic imprint are not printed in the supplied text, so these details cannot be independently confirmed here. No PDF path was supplied. Only n_o is assigned; other fields/sides are null placeholders. Target correspondence remains unresolved: manuscript p. 5 is theoretical introduction rather than a results locator. Candidate tests are the five-condition mixed ANOVA (p. 10/Table 1); Conditions 1 and 3 versus 2 and 4 relearning interaction F(1, 190) = 10.49, p < .001 (pp. 11–12); before/after relearning t(95) = 2.79, p < .01 and t(95) = 1.84, p = .07 (p. 12); and Condition 5 interaction F(1, 47) = 8.30, p < .01 (pp. 12–13). These printed statistics are candidate context only, not assigned effects. The total 240 is explicitly an experiment participation count. No mutually exclusive final group counts are printed, so no analytic N sum is supported. No N has been inferred from degrees of freedom. Even the likely Conditions 1–4 interaction does not have an explicit printed analytic N. No acquisition performed.
